one_liner: Auto-tuned mixed-precision GPU GEMV/GEMM (FP16/INT8 activations x INT4/INT2/INT1/NF4/FP4/FP8 weights) that beats FP16 cuBLAS by moving fewer bytes.
what_it_does: A Python library that generates and tunes CUDA kernels for C = A x W^T where activations and weights use different dtypes, aimed at quantized LLM inference (GPTQ W_UINT4 A_FP16, BitNet b1.58 W_INT2 A_INT8, NF4, FP8). You describe the operation with bitblas.MatmulConfig (M, N, K, dtypes, layout 'nt', group size, scaling, zeros mode) and call bitblas.Matmul, or use bitblas.Linear as an nn.Linear-like module; weights must first go through transform_weight / load_and_transform_weight into BitBLAS's packed layout. Integration examples exist for vLLM, AutoGPTQ, GPTQModel and BitNet.
how_it_is_fast: It implements Ladder (OSDI'24): low-bit weights are stored packed and dequantized on the fly inside the tensor-core GEMM, so a memory-bound GEMV reads 4-16x fewer bytes than FP16. Weights are pre-permuted offline ('ladder permutate' into ldmatrix-friendly layouts, and 'lop3 permutate' so dequantization uses LOP3 bit tricks, fast_decoding), which removes layout shuffles and cheapens unpacking. Kernels are generated by TVM TIR or TileLang schedulers and tuned per shape and GPU, with dynamic-M kernels built for an opt_M list such as [1, 16, 32, 64, 128].
when_to_use: Memory-bound LLM decode (batch 1 to small batches) with weight-only quantization (INT4/NF4/INT2) on Ampere or Ada NVIDIA GPUs (A100, A6000, RTX 3090/4090 are the tested platforms).
Unusual format pairs that hand-written kernels lack: INT8 x INT2/INT1 (BitNet b1.58), INT4 x INT4, FP16 x FP4/FP8, BF16 x NF4.
Research on new quantization formats, where you need a kernel for a dtype combination without writing CUDA (TIR/TileLang DSL customization).
A frozen deployment where you can pre-tune kernels once and load them from BitBLAS's on-disk operator database.
when_not_to_use: New production work: the repo was archived on 2026-02-24 (last commit 2025-05-05) and open wrong-result bug reports will not be fixed.
FP16 x FP16 or INT8 x INT8 GEMM alone: the benchmark README only claims to match cuBLAS/CUTLASS there.
Hopper or Blackwell GPUs: the README support matrix has no sm_90 or newer row (tested platforms are V100, A100, A6000 and RTX 4090), so performance there is not documented.
Latency-sensitive startup: the QuickStart says bitblas.Matmul initialization 'will take minutes' for a one-time kernel library build per configuration.
Non-Linux hosts or Python-free C++ use: wheels are Ubuntu 20.04+ only, and the kernels are reached through a Python/TVM runtime.

integration.dependencies: PyTorch, a bundled TVM fork and TileLang (3rdparty, built with CMake against a downloaded LLVM 10.0.1 when building from source), CUDA toolkit >= 11.0, plus numpy, scipy, tornado, cloudpickle, ml_dtypes and others from requirements.txt
integration.min_toolchain: Python >= 3.8 and CUDA >= 11.0 for the PyPI wheel (Ubuntu 20.04+); source build needs CMake, gcc and LLVM
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 with NVIDIA GPUs; tested on V100 (sm_70), A100 (sm_80), A6000 (sm_86), RTX 4090 (sm_89); FP8 and INT4xINT4 only on sm_89. The OSDI artifact branch also lists an AMD MI250, and an install_amd.sh script exists (issue #298), but the main README support matrix is NVIDIA-only
integration.thread_safety: partial — the global OperatorCache guards its dict with a threading.RLock; concurrent kernel calls are otherwise not documented (kernels launch on torch.cuda.current_stream)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — bitblas.Linear mimics nn.Linear, but weights must be repacked with load_and_transform_weight, and it replaces cuBLAS only through its own Matmul/Linear API, not as a BLAS-compatible library

gotchas: Open, unanswered correctness bugs in the formats the headline claim is about: #316 (W_INT2 A_INT8 Matmul, 0.1.0.post1) gives 6.2% mismatched elements (max abs diff 19,645) on the first call but correct results later, which the reporter attributes to a different kernel being selected; #313 reports wrong values from a W_INT4 A_INT8 Linear on an RTX 4090.
#296 (open): bitblas.Linear with uint4 weights and with_scaling=True leads to a CUDA illegal memory access.
Inputs whose M is not in opt_M run the next-larger tuned kernel (an M of 15 uses the M=16 kernel), so performance between tuned points is not what the plots show.

The 8x/2x A100 claim compares W_INT2 A_INT8 against W_FP16 A_FP16 cuBLAS, so most of the gain comes from moving fewer bytes and depends on the model tolerating 2-bit weights; the PyPI release (0.1.0.post1, 2025-02-16) lags the repo, and the OSDI artifact lives on a separate TVM-based branch.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick BitBLAS over Marlin when you need weight formats other than FP16 x INT4 (INT2/INT1/NF4/FP4/FP8, or INT8 activations), or shape coverage beyond small batches; for plain GPTQ INT4 inference Marlin is a smaller, single-purpose kernel that is not archived. T-MAC and BitNet (bitnet.cpp) are the CPU counterparts for the same low-bit LLM workloads.
verified_claims_summary: First-party plots on an RTX 3090 and an A100-80GB with CUDA 12.1 (third-party baselines pinned by commit: bitsandbytes 0.43.0, vLLM, FasterTransformer, TensorRT-LLM, CUTLASS and Marlin, reproduced via the separate mlc-benchmark repo) show FP16/INT8 tensor-core GEMM matching cuBLAS/CUTLASS, FP16 x NF4 at 2x bitsandbytes and 4x FP16, and W_INT2 A_INT8 GEMV/GEMM at 8x/2x over FP16 cuBLAS on A100 for BLOOM/OPT/LLaMA layer shapes. The peer-reviewed Ladder paper (OSDI'24) covers the TVM-based artifact branch, not the later TileLang release, and all numbers are in images, not text.
status_note: Archived by Microsoft on 2026-02-24 (last commit 2025-05-05, PyPI 0.1.0.post1 from 2025-02-16); MIT-licensed and usable as a frozen dependency or reference for Ladder-style layout transforms, but bugs will not be fixed.
